translation:
Wild chrysanthemum, crested iris (shan-ci-gu), cohosh (sheng-ma, roasted on tile), and dragon's blood (each 1 qian 5 fen). Trichosanthes powder 1 qian. Paris polyphylla (qi-ye-yi-zhi-hua), Viola herb, wood-ear fungus, and locust-pod spine (zao-jiao-ci, each roasted on tile), and cinnabar (water-levigated clean) (each 3 qian). Sichuan fritillaria bulb (heart removed), and anemarrhena (zhi-mu, each roasted on tile, or it may instead be boiled through in yellow wine and baked dry), and venom of toad (chan-su, each 3 qian, dissolved in wine, kept raw without seeing fire), licorice and musk (each 5 fen). Castor-seed flesh 1 liang (husk and skin removed, mashed for use).

Of the above drugs, excepting the six flavors of musk, toad-venom, dragon's blood, castor flesh, and cinnabar, roast the rest on tile preserving their nature. Together with the preceding drugs, grind into a very fine powder and pound with the castor flesh into a mash as an ointment. If it becomes dry, add Shandong rouge; if none is available, sesame oil will also do. When using, first prick open the root of the furuncle (ding) with a silver needle, put a little of this ointment into it, and cover it with a pair of medicinal plasters. After a full day (zhou-shi) the furuncle draws itself out.

A secret formula that treats scrofula (luo-li) and phlegm-kernels (tan-he).

Pangolin scales, scorpion, angelica dahurica, golden thread, whole angelica, and scutellaria (each 2 liang). Rehmannia, red peony, and strychnos shell (each 1 liang). Cassia-bark twig and seaweed (each 4 liang).

Using 2 jin 4 liang of sesame oil in a pot, boil the above dry, discard the dregs and purify; add 10 liang of minium (fei-dan), 7 qian of yellow wax, 3 qian of white wax, and 2 liang of lead powder; collect the ointment, throw it into water to soak, take it out, and air-dry. Then melt it again in a pot; add frankincense, myrrh, and calomel (each 2 qian), musk, realgar, and cinnabar (each 1 qian), north-facing swallow-nest mud and male-rat droppings (each 5 qian), and dragon's blood 1 liang; grind all into a fine powder, take it off the fire, put it into the previous ointment, stir evenly, and store.

One black cat, of whatever size, but it must be one that died from being bitten by a dog; use it whole, together with its fur, hide, intestines, and stomach.

Boil and dissolve the above in sesame oil, strain out the dregs, and decoct the oil until a dropped drop forms a pearl; add yellow minium to collect the plaster, and spread it on the affected area. The effect is miraculous.
